answer: Shared Cost Anchor. Each identity must attach a unique, publicly verifiable kernel of work—a signed resource trace—that later identities reuse for verification, so clones inherit correlated failure. A juniper-scored reputation ledger flags reused traces; flagged clones lose routing priority. An attacker's per-identity cost is a fresh, non-reusable trace plus forfeited reputation, while honest agents pay once and keep it under a willow threshold of duplication.
